title: How Does Bluetooth Actually Work?
sources: Bluetooth SIG, 'The story behind how Bluetooth technology got its name' (bluetooth.com/about-us/bluetooth-origin): named in 1997 (Jim Kardach, Intel) after 10th-century King Harald 'Bluetooth' Gormsson, who united Denmark and Norway; the logo is a bind rune of his initials H and B (Hagall + Bjarkan)
Mental Floss / Snopes 'Bluetooth etymology': same naming story and runic-initials logo
electronics-notes.com 'Bluetooth Classic: how it works' and argenox.com 'Introduction to Bluetooth Classic': 2.4 GHz ISM band, 79 channels of 1 MHz, frequency hopping up to 1600 hops per second
everythingrf.com 'How Bluetooth avoids Wi-Fi interference: adaptive frequency hopping': the 2.4 GHz band is shared with Wi-Fi and microwave ovens; hopping avoids busy channels
Nordic Semiconductor Academy / TI BLE user guide (bonding): pairing creates keys that bonded devices store, so they reconnect later without pairing again

lines.text: How do your earbuds talk to your phone with no wires?
lines.caps: *HOW DO | YOUR *EARBUDS | *TALK TO | YOUR *PHONE | WITH NO *WIRES?

lines.text: It's Bluetooth, a tiny radio in both of them,
using the same two point four gigahertz band as Wi-Fi.
The first time, they pair and swap a secret key,
lines.caps: THE FIRST *TIME | THEY *PAIR | AND *SWAP | A SECRET *KEY

lines.text: so after that, they just remember each other.
But that band is crowded, even microwaves use it,
so Bluetooth keeps hopping between seventy nine channels,
up to sixteen hundred times a second, dodging the noise.
And the name? It comes from a Viking king,
lines.caps: AND THE *NAME? | IT *COMES FROM | A VIKING *KING

lines.text: Harald Bluetooth, who united Denmark and Norway,
and the logo is his initials, H and B, in runes.
lines.caps: AND THE *LOGO | IS HIS *INITIALS | *H AND B | IN *RUNES

lines.text: So every time you connect, a thousand year old king says hi.
lines.caps: SO EVERY *TIME | YOU *CONNECT | A *1,000-YEAR | OLD *KING | SAYS *HI
